Harvey (ethanplusai/harvey) - fit for th.summary:
RECOMMENDATION: do not run Harvey against the Database app. Treat it as an MIT-licensed design reference and, at most, a manual, read-only, human-approved "score and enrich" helper. Build the 0-100 ICP score and the country/state time-zone logic natively in Database, and add an optional "Ask Harvey" button that only suggests a score and a note and never acts.

1) What Harvey is. It is an autonomous cold-email sales agent: a Python 3.11+ CLI, a SQLite database and a loopback-only FastAPI dashboard. Every 15 minutes it discovers businesses, profiles their websites, finds the owner, verifies the email, writes a 3-email sequence, sends it from your own mailbox (Gmail, M365, SMTP or Instantly), reads replies and handles them. The MIT clone is at D:\All Automations Records\Harvey, HEAD 6b6a23a (2026-11-01), version 0.3.0, working tree clean. It has no Google Sheets reader and no lead-import or HTTP ingest path. It only exports CSV, and its data model is companies and prospects, where a prospect needs a first name, last name and title. So it cannot ingest Database's leads without custom glue.

2) Parts worth borrowing, as ideas or small ports rather than the runtime:
- harvey/fit.py is a deterministic 0-100 company fit score with human-readable reasons. The weights are sector 20, decision-maker title 30, reachable email 25 and buying signal 25. It is computed on read, nothing is stored, and it follows the config at once. This maps directly onto "lead quality score vs ICP", and I recommend it as the template for Database's score.
- harvey/send_window.py has zone_for(location, country, point). It resolves an IANA time zone from a US state, Canadian province, Australian state or country, using state tables and pytz. It is pure local code with no network, and it is a ready reference for the country/state/time-zone report.
- The agents/scout.py _score_contacts pattern asks an LLM to score a batch 1-100 and write a note, returns JSON, falls back to a heuristic if the model fails, and wraps untrusted text with harvey/untrusted.py. It fits an optional "score and summarise" step.
- The "every fact is a row" observations model (signal, value, confidence, evidence URL, observed_at) suits enrichment and history.
- Email normalisation as the dedupe key.

3) Integration options, safest first:
- (A, recommended) Native Database code only. This is the fit.py-style score plus the time-zone table, with no LLM and no Harvey process.
- (B, optional) An "Ask Harvey" button on a lead or a selected batch. It is a Database server function that calls the Anthropic API with an API key (Haiku-class model), using Scout's prompt and fence pattern. It stores a suggestion (score, note, timestamp, who clicked) in a separate table, shows it to the admin, and never writes back to Google Sheets and never triggers outbound.
- (C, only if the real Harvey code must be used) A separate local worker that pulls leads from a read-only Database service token, scores them, and posts back only score and note to a write-limited endpoint. Harvey's mail, LinkedIn, Instantly and discovery parts stay unconfigured and sending stays paused.
- Not recommended: Harvey as a library inside the Database app. It is tied to its own SQLite schema, its Claude CLI "Brain" and a single-user model.
- Not recommended: any autonomous Harvey run (heartbeat plus sender) pointed at Database leads.

4) Main risk: the Claude subscription. Harvey's brain is `claude -p` using your Claude Pro/Max login, with no API key. Anthropic's legal page (checked 2026-11-04) says subscription OAuth is "designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications", and that developers building products should use API-key auth. It also says Anthropic does not permit routing requests through Free/Pro/Max credentials on behalf of users, and that advertised limits "assume ordinary, individual usage". Consumer Terms section 3 item 7 bars "automated or non-human" access except via API key or with Anthropic's explicit permission. Harvey runs the unmodified `claude` binary, so for one operator it is a grey zone and not a clear breach. A multi-user dashboard that re-scores leads every 1-2 minutes is not ordinary individual use. Anthropic has no explicit statement on `claude -p` under a subscription, so use an API key for anything the Database app triggers.

5) Other risks:
- Autonomous outbound is Harvey's whole purpose. It is guarded by require_approval: true (default), a 50/day cap, quiet hours and a pre-send gate. But autopilot is one config line or a typed word in Settings, and a CLAUDE.md in the repo makes Claude Code act as the setup wizard when you open that folder.
- It reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json and calls the undocumented api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage (quota.py). Codex mode reads ~/.codex/auth.json.
- It scrapes search-engine HTML (DuckDuckGo, Bing, Google) and company websites. LinkedIn automation is off by default and the README itself says it breaches LinkedIn's ToS.
- Optional third-party calls send lead data out if keys are set: Precleared (recipient email, names, product text), Hunter, Reoon, ZeroBounce, Serper, DataForSEO and TrulyInbox.
- No telemetry and no shell=True/eval were found.
- Prompt injection from lead fields is mitigated by fencing but the repo itself says it is not guaranteed.

6) Scan and registry. SkillSpector gave 100/100 CRITICAL "DO NOT INSTALL", but it was a static-only scan with the semantic analyzers disabled. 223 issues: most of the HIGH ones are PE3 credential-path matches in docs and tests, plus a handful of test-file false positives. The real findings are the Codex auth.json read and an anti-refusal line in skills/sales_methodology.md. The hub registry verdict is CAUTION ("legal/account risk, not malware"), installed with user approval on 2026-11-03. The email-automation BRIEF says "Borrow ideas, not the app".

7) Cost and fit. There is no model API bill under the subscription path, but the budget gate will use up to 80% of the daily quota (max_daily_claude_percent) and compete with your own Claude Code use. Real money goes to a mailbox (about $7/mo), an email verifier, search and discovery APIs, and TrulyInbox (from $22/mo billed yearly, an affiliate link the repo pushes). The stack is Python, SQLite and vanilla-JS, with one operator and one token. That does not match Database's roles, per-sheet access and single-session standard, so a UI or auth port is pointless. It is also pre-1.0 and changes fast: the repo's own changelog says "minor versions can still change behaviour".

facts.fact: Data model: SQLite data/harvey.db. Tables companies, prospects, campaigns, conversations, outbox, actions, runs, usage_events, email_patterns, settings, feedback, observations, signal_codes. Prospect needs first_name, last_name, title; has phone, timezone, score, email_status (verified/risky/guess/invalid). Company has name, domain, industry, location, tech_stack, signals. There is no 'niche' or 'state' field; signals are agency/SEO-specific (INCUMBENT_AGENCY, NO_ONLINE_BOOKING, RUNNING_GOOGLE_ADS, SERP_RANK ...).

fit.py scores a company 0-100 with reasons: sector 20, decision maker 30 (15 for another named person, 5 for general inbox), reachable 25 (verified 25, risky 12, guess 5, contact form 5), buying signal 25 (hiring role match; 5 for careers page with no match); do-not-contact scores 0; computed on read and never stored.

Scout LLM scoring: batch prompt asks for JSON [{index, score 1-100, personalization}] given ICP industries/titles/size, wraps scraped text in an <untrusted> fence, seeds a heuristic baseline (base 40, +25 title match, seniority and industry bonuses), falls back to the heuristic if the model fails, drops scores below 30. Notes capped at 500 chars. Scout prompt says missing info should lower scores and forbids fabricated details.
untrusted.py fences external text (NFKC fold, zero-width strip, tag removal) and the module itself states this 'makes a model less likely to follow planted instructions. It is not a guarantee'.

send_window.zone_for(location, country, point) resolves an IANA zone from a US state (US_STATES), Canadian province, Australian state, a single-zone country, or cached coordinates, with a MAIN_ZONE fallback for multi-zone countries; uses pytz country names and zone.tab, no network.
The README says Harvey is worth running as a list-builder even if it never sends, and `harvey export` writes a sequencer-ready CSV (verified/risky only; --all for raw).

Costs per the README/CLAUDE.md: no model API bill (uses Claude Pro/Max or ChatGPT plan); discovery free on OpenStreetMap/TinyFish, paid options from about $0.002-$0.37 per 1k/search; mailbox about $7/mo (Google Workspace); TrulyInbox warmup API access from $22/mo billed yearly (affiliate link ?via=harvey; CLAUDE.md Step 2b tells Claude to recommend it); verifier free tiers (Reoon 600/mo, ZeroBounce 100/mo, Hunter 50/mo) are README claims. pitfalls: DIFFERENT - direction and shape: the CRM sync WRITES a DB mirror to one Sheet and clears/overwrites whole tabs each run. Database must READ many sheets that automations append to, and must never write to or clear those sheets. Use the readonly scope, share lead sheets as Viewer.

DIFFERENT - 2-minute scans vs quotas: CRM reads the whole tab every run (google.ts:89-92). At */2 cron = 21,600 invocations/month per function (720/day x 30), versus 500,000/month Free; one invocation per sheet each tick would cap at ~23 sheets. Scan ALL due sheets in ONE invocation (round-robin by last_scanned_at), stay under 150 s wall-clock (Free) and 2 s CPU per request, and keep Google reads under 60/min/user (about 120 spreadsheets per 2-min tick at most, fewer with metadata calls; whether a service account counts as the 'user' is not verified).

DIFFERENT - incremental reads: store per-sheet cursor (last row read / row count / header hash) and request only new rows (batchGet with a row range); dedupe with a stable key (sheet_id + row_number or a content hash) using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A whole-tab re-read plus whole-table rewrite like the CRM will blow the 2 MB payload guidance and the CPU limit once sheets reach thousands of rows.

DIFFERENT - failure isolation: CRM has a single try/catch and one last_status row. Database needs per-sheet status rows (last_scan_at, last_status, last_error, consecutive_failures, rows_seen), Promise.allSettled-style isolation so one unshared/deleted sheet (403/404) does not stop the others, and visible alerts in the admin UI.

DIFFERENT - overlap protection: nothing in the CRM stops a slow run overlapping the next tick (no lock). With 1-2 minute ticks and a 150 s Free wall-clock, runs WILL overlap. Add a lease row (locked_until) or a claim-style 'select ... for update skip locked' on due sheets. pg_net is fire-and-forget: a failed or timed-out call is not retried by pg_cron.

DIFFERENT - admin cap: the CRM only has a floor (keep_one_admin) and NO maximum. Database needs a configurable ceiling (default 2): a setting row (max_admins) read by a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger on profiles that counts active admins under a row lock (copy the FOR UPDATE trick from migration 13 lines 165-170) and refuses the 3rd; also surface a clear error in admin-users set_role and the Team UI; decide whether the owner counts toward the cap and whether lowering max_admins below the current count is refused.

DIFFERENT - per-sheet access: CRM visibility is per-task (visible_task_ids via assignees/watchers/teams). Database needs a sheet_access(sheet_id, user_id) table plus a private.accessible_sheet_ids() SECURITY DEFINER helper in the same style, and RLS on leads/reports keyed to it; lead assignment adds a second path (assigned_to).

DIFFERENT - delete approval: CRM employees simply cannot delete (policy removed in 0011). Database wants 'employees may add, may not remove without admin approval': keep delete policy admin-only, add a deletion_requests table (target table/id, reason, requested_by, status pending/approved/rejected, decided_by, decided_at) that employees may INSERT only for rows they can see, and an admin-only RPC that approves and performs the delete in one transaction with an audit row. The CRM report review flow (draft -> submitted -> approved/revision_requested, guard_report_review) is the closest pattern.

Audit volume: write_audit stores full old/new JSONB per row. Attached to a leads table that the scanner fills every 1-2 minutes it would double storage against the 500 MB Free cap and spam the log. Audit admin/employee actions (UPDATE/DELETE, assignments, access, requests, config), not scanner INSERTs (service_role has auth.uid() null, so performed_by would be null anyway).

Realtime volume: the CRM refetches everything on any change (DataContext.tsx:263-269). A bulk scan insert emits one Realtime message per row (Free: 2M messages/month, 200 concurrent connections). For live reports broadcast a single 'scan finished' tick row (e.g. sheet_scan_runs) and have clients refetch aggregates.

ICP (ideal client profile) and lead-qual.area: ICP (ideal client profile) and lead-quality rules, for the Database app's 0-10 lead-quality score
ICP (ideal client profile) and lead-qual.summary:
1) The user's "lead quality 7/10" already exists in code: the lead bot writes `ICP Score /10` and refuses to add any lead below `MIN_ICP_SCORE` = 7 (defaults.py L162). Tiers are A >= 8.5, B >= 7.5, else C. The score is "10 = perfect client who pays $1k/month at the first meeting". Money targets are in the same rules: business leads 500-1000/mo, YouTube creators 1000-2000/mo, in `PITCH_CURRENCY` (default AUD, one value per sheet).
2) Because of that gate, every business lead in the sheets is already >= 7.0 by construction. Only the HAS-AGENCY and POLISHED-NO-SIGNAL "side" segments skip it (they need R >= 6). A Database chart of ICP score alone will be flat and will not measure "quality vs ICP". See the proposal below.
3) The score is a formula (quality.py `icp3`): revenue proxy R 35, social gap 25, niche budget fit 15, contactability 15, decision maker 5, Google rating 3, location 2, minus up to 15 for agency likelihood. Segments (PRIME, PRIME-REVIEW, GROWING, HAS-AGENCY, POLISHED-NO-SIGNAL) come from R (revenue proxy 0-10), S (social strength 0-10) and A (agency confidence 0-100). Every threshold is an editable Rules key. Caveat: YouTube leads still use the older v3 formula (score.py `score`, W2_* weights), so one sheet column holds two formulas.
4) Who the ideal client is, from code and rules: owner-run, mid-sized, high-ticket local businesses with 8-600 Google reviews, rating >= 3.5, a website, NOT a chain (same name or site in 3+ places = chain) and NOT already served by an agency. Seeded niches carry a Budget Fit of 1-5. Enabled niches: surgeons, dentists, skin clinics, hair transplant, independent real estate, buyers agents, mortgage brokers, accountants, migration and law firms, furniture, kitchen and bath showrooms, jewellers, car and boat dealers, custom builders and architects, solar, pools and landscaping, wedding venues, private colleges and childcare, boutique hotels, fine dining, boutique gyms. YouTube creators: 20k-500k subscribers (sweet spot 20k-250k), last upload within 14 days, median views >= 20k, countries AU/US/GB/CA/NZ/IE/AE (blank country allowed). Revenue is only a Low/Mid/High band (under 15k, 15k-60k, over 60k per month), never a number to quote.
5) Disqualifiers are hard-coded (see facts): chain or big-brand name lists, public bodies, schools and hospitals, not operating, too few or too many reviews, low rating, ABN cancelled, blacklisted, no contact route (YouTube also needs an email), and agency or in-house team found (A >= 50). The outreach bot also never cold-pitches HAS-AGENCY or POLISHED-NO-SIGNAL (generate.py L458).
6) Email and name rules: generic mailboxes (info@, hello@) are NOT disqualified anywhere. They are a Generic fallback scored 0.65 vs 0.85 for a Personal address, +0.1 if verified, -0.1 if catch-all. System addresses (noreply, postmaster, abuse, billing, careers and similar), placeholder domains, bad syntax and no-MX domains are rejected. Free-mail (gmail etc.) is skipped for GB/IE only and flagged for CA. First names are optional: used only if the Decision Maker Name is a verified fact (titles stripped, brands and role words rejected), else "Hi <Company> team," (outreach bot) or "Hi Team," (local drafter). Only about 20-35% of free-source leads have a decision maker.
7) "Hard ceiling" is NOT defined for lead intake or quality anywhere I read. The phrase appears for send limits: Gmail 70/day and domain 650/day (original prompt said 700), safe band 60/600 (SCHEMA.md L40, L126), inbox cap 50 (generate.py L469), and the UI label "Hard ceiling = Maximum allowed" (DESIGN.md L34). Lead-supply caps also exist (NEW_LEADS_PER_RUN 120, IMPORT_LEADS_PER_RUN 300, Google Sheets 10M-cell limit with a stop at 9.5M). The user must say which one they meant.
8) PROPOSAL for the Database score (not in any file, needs the user's OK): if a row has `ICP Score /10`, show it unchanged and band it (A/B/C, below 7 = off-target). For sheets without it (other automations, imports), compute a fallback 0-10 from mapped columns, renormalised over the fields present (the same trick as quality.py L106-118): niche budget fit 3.0, contactability 2.5 (personal non-role email on own domain 0.85, generic 0.65, social or phone only 0.2, verified +0.1, risky -0.1, invalid or bounced = 0), country in target list 1.5 (blank = neutral), verified decision maker or first name 1.0, size or reputation 1.5 (reviews 8-600 and rating >= 3.5, or YouTube 20k-500k), website or social 0.5. Cap at 6.0 for chain-name or HAS-AGENCY leads; 0 if there is no email and no social. Add dashboard KPIs: percent at or above 7, average ICP, Tier A/B/C counts, percent with a personal email, percent with a decision maker, percent with a verified email.
9) Not checked: the AU-only twin's market.py, ig-outreach (no ICP found by grep), SAMPLE_LEADS csv, any live sheet. Nothing was run. I did not open Keys, all-info, .env, secrets or zip files.

pitfalls: Score saturation: the lead bot refuses to write business leads below ICP 7.0, so a histogram of `ICP Score /10` in the sheets is flat (7.0-10). Quality KPIs must be ratios and bands (Tier A/B/C, share >= 8.5, share with personal email) or a different measure, not 'how many are above 7'.

One column, two formulas: YouTube rows use the v3 formula (W2_* weights), business rows use v4 (W3_*); pre-v4 rows also use v3 and have a blank Segment. Do not compare ICP across niches or eras without noting this.
Side segments (HAS-AGENCY, POLISHED-NO-SIGNAL) can have ICP < 7 and are never cold-pitched; decide whether they count in 'leads today' and in quality KPIs.
Do not require Country (blank on YouTube rows), First Name (only ~20-35% coverage), or Personal Email (many leads have only a generic one). A score that demands them would zero most real leads.
Pitch Currency is per row and defaults to AUD while the user speaks of USD/AUD: never sum 'Suggested Pitch /mo' across currencies without converting or grouping.
'Lead Added On' is written in each sheet's own Rules TIMEZONE (default UTC), so 'leads today' per sheet can disagree with the admin's clock; read each sheet's TIMEZONE or ask.

Lead sheets are append-only and Status/My Notes belong to the lead bot contract and the user: the Database must not write into lead tabs by default. Skip control tabs (Master Dashboard, Stats, Seen, Snapshots, Blacklist, OLD *) or counts will be inflated.
The same lead can appear in two sheets only if Place Ids differ; the contract dedupes per sheet, not across sheets. Cross-sheet dedupe by email needs the Database to do it.
Revenue Band and Suggested Pitch are proxy estimates ('free signals (unverified)' rows exist); label them as estimates and never show them as facts.

Hard-coded numbers disagree across bots (YouTube min subs 20k vs 15k, max 500k vs none, last upload 14 vs 21 days, tier-1 countries 7 vs 6, hard cap NEW_LEADS_PER_RUN 60 in old doc vs 120 in code). Do not hard-code ICP values in the Database; make them admin settings.

Importer reads Sheets with a read-only service account: GoogleSheets uses GOOGLE_SA_JSON (file path or JSON) with scope spreadsheets.readonly, one values call per tab (FORMATTED_VALUE, so dates and numbers arrive as displayed strings) plus metadata calls for title and tab list, retrying 429/5xx up to 5 times with backoff min(60, 2^attempt*2) seconds. The SheetSource protocol (title, tabs, values) has a FixtureSheets JSON backend for tests and dry runs. Setup: share each sheet with the service account email as Viewer, then insert into sources (sheet_id, tab_name), where tab_name '*' means every lead tab. The in-app Sources screen is only a mock (ImportSheet), so source rows are inserted by SQL today.

Column auto-detection (no header setup): detect_header scans the first 10 rows and picks the row with the most known header words (needs at least 2 hits; data-looking cells count against a row). map_columns reads up to 50 non-empty body rows and assigns one candidate per column: user override (1.0) beats exact alias (0.95), which beats fuzzy alias (difflib ratio >= 0.85, scored 0.8). Unmapped columns are then sniffed by content: email (>= 50% of cells hold an address), website (non-social URL), country (value resolves to US/CA/AU). 25 canonical fields: email, personal_email, other_emails, name, first_name, company, website, youtube, instagram, facebook, tiktok, linkedin, niche, city, region, country, country_code, phone, insight, latest_video, subscribers, score, status, source_url, notes. A word may belong to only one field (asserted at import). An email-named column with under 30% addresses is demoted to confidence 0.3.

Tab handling: a tab with email confidence below 0.6 (MIN_EMAIL_CONFIDENCE) is skipped, with last_error saved on its sources row and an 'import_mapping' alert (never a guess). Tabs ignored by name: blacklist, run log, playbook, niches, rules, dashboard, anything starting 'old '; a tab named Blacklist is loaded into suppression. Each tab keeps its own header_row, detected_mapping (field, column, confidence, by) and mapping_override. Per-row skips are counted: blank, stop_word (status cell says no/false/inactive/dead/closed/stop/unsubscribed/replied/bounced/invalid/dnc/blocked/sent), no_valid_email, unusable_email. Unmapped columns are preserved in leads.extra_data as {header: value}.

Two differently structured sheets are covered by a test: fixture_au_bot (header on row 0, columns Place Id / Company Name / Decision Maker Name / Personal Email / Generic Email / Other Emails / Niche / Country / City..., plus Blacklist and Run Log tabs, registered once with tab_name '*') and fixture_messy (sheet titled 'Canada Restaurants Data', title rows above, header on row index 3 with 'E-Mail Address', 'State / Province', 'Active?', no Country column). Both import with no configuration: 9 leads, 1 duplicate, 2 stop-word skips; the messy sheet gets header_row 3 and its mapping is saved on the sources row. Country evidence order: country column, country_code column, region, phone (+61, or +1 with a Canadian area code), website or email TLD, then tab name and sheet name only when the tab has no country column.

canonical_email dedupe: emails.canonical() lowercases, removes any +tag (every domain), removes dots for gmail.com and maps googlemail.com to gmail.com; leads.canonical_email is UNIQUE with a lowercase check. insert_leads dedupes inside the batch (first row wins), checks existing leads and suppression, then INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (canonical_email) DO NOTHING, so a re-run inserts zero. Extra holds: same business domain (freemail excluded) and recently contacted address. Addresses are validated (blocked local parts like noreply, fake/disposable domains, role addresses flagged).

Import cadence: the engine tick runs every minute (systemd timer, one advisory lock) and the 'import' phase is registered with every_minutes=150 (due when the last OK run_log row is older than N minutes). Each run re-reads EVERY row of EVERY enabled tab and relies on the unique key to skip duplicates; sources.last_imported_row is written but never used to skip rows. The importer only inserts: the module header says later edits in the sheet are ignored and the leads table is the truth, so edited or removed rows are never synced.

Google Sheets API quota (official docs): read requests 300 per minute per project and 60 per minute per user per project; same for writes; over the limit returns HTTP 429, retry with exponential backoff (2^n seconds plus up to 1 s random, capped around 32-64 s). At Outreach's cost of one values call per tab, scanning N tabs every minute uses N calls per minute, so the 60-per-user cap binds first on a single credential.

Drive API v3 files resource has modifiedTime (last modified by anyone), version (output-only, monotonically increasing, 'reflects every change made to the file on the server') and modifiedByMeTime; headRevisionId is only for binary files so it is not available for Sheets. The docs do not explicitly say a cell edit bumps modifiedTime or version, so that must be tested before using it for cheap change detection (one files.get per sheet per scan instead of one values call per tab).

Lead schema (database): leads has id, email, canonical_email (UNIQUE), email_hash, email_domain, first_name, company, website, youtube_url, phone (raw text, no E.164 normalisation), city, region (state/province code), country_code (2 letters, null = unknown), country_source, niche, niche_confidence, tz (IANA, validated by app.is_tz, null = unknown), tz_uncertain, source_id, source_row, source_url, latest_video, angle, low_data, style_index, email_check, extra_data jsonb (unmapped columns plus subscribers and score), status/hold_reason/stop_reason, notes, imported_at, updated_at. sources has sheet_id, sheet_title, tab_name, enabled, header_row, detected_mapping, mapping_override, email_confidence, last_imported_row, last_import_at, rows_imported, last_error, UNIQUE(sheet_id, tab_name). The sheet's own lead score is stored raw in extra_data.score and never parsed or compared with an ICP.

Time zone resolution (engine): geo.timezone(country, region, city) returns (IANA zone, uncertain). It uses a region-to-zone table for US states, Canadian provinces and Australian states, a CITY_ZONES exception list for split regions (e.g. TX El Paso America/Denver, ON Kenora America/Winnipeg), the country default zone when the region is unknown (uncertain), and (None, True) for any country other than US, CA or AU (TARGETS). No other country has a zone table. region_code() normalises state names/codes; country_from_value() normalises country names, ISO codes and aliases for ~35 countries.

Time zone display code that works for any IANA zone: fmtLeadTime(iso, tz) gives '10:43 AM EST'; fmtZone uses en-AU names for Australia (en-US prints 'GMT+11'); fmtWeekday, fmtDate, fmtDateShort and fmtDateTimePkt take a time zone; APP_TZ is Asia/Karachi (PKT). leads/format.ts adds localNow(tz) and whenLocal(iso, tz). mocks/leads.ts has localYmd, localMinutes, zonedToUtc (wall-clock minutes on a date in a zone to a UTC instant) and addBusinessDays on a cached Intl.DateTimeFormat. The Leads table 'Where' cell shows 'City, ST' plus '<local time> there now'. DESIGN.md rule: every clock time names whose it is (PKT or the lead's zone); calendar-day totals say 'Pakistan time'.

Report-day logic for today / this week / this month: lib/workday.ts holds {tz, dayStart} (default Asia/Karachi, 00:00), workdayDate(iso) names the day by the date it started, periodNote() prints what a period covers, weeks start Monday. Roles and permissions in Outreach: profiles.role is admin or employee. Login standard: email + password, optional Google button (off until Supabase). One active session per account is built in the database (Supabase's own feature is Pro-only): active_sessions has one row per user whose session_id equals the JWT session_id claim; app.is_member() is true only while they match, so an older session instantly sees no rows; claim_session(user_agent) is called right after sign-in; session_status() returns ok, replaced, inactive, signed_out or change_password. Path legend used in all sources: ROOT = D:\All Automations Records ; LB = ROOT\Lead generation\au-lead-bot (worldwide lead bot, v5; the nested au-lead-bot\au-lead-bot copy has identical src/) ; AU = ROOT\Lead generation\au-only-lead-bot ; IG = ROOT\Insta outreach Automation\ig-outreach ; ORG = ROOT\Figma Organizer\sheet-organizer ; LD = ROOT\Local Draft File ; FC = ROOT\Full Cycle Emails Outreach File.

1) The only real lead producer is the lead bot (two editions, one codebase; only src/market.py differs). Worldwide writes up to 10 separate Google Sheets (US, CA, GB, AU, NZ, IE, optional AE, SA, QA, plus one worldwide YOUTUBE sheet); the AU-only edition writes one sheet. Each sheet = one tab per niche (the data tabs) + a Stats dashboard tab (tab 1; the US sheet also holds the 'Master Dashboard' as tab 1 and 'US Stats' as tab 2) + a hidden 'Meta' tab + control tabs (Rules, Niches, Locations, Seen, Searches, Snapshots, Blacklist, Run Log, Options, Playbook, Import, Leads Input). Lead tabs must be detected by header (row 1 has both 'Place Id' and 'Company Name'), never by name; users may rename tabs and reorder columns.
2) Lead tabs have 74 columns (worldwide) or 82 (AU: +8 ABN/AU columns). Core mapping targets: Company Name, Decision Maker Name/First Name/Role, Personal Email / Generic Email / Other Emails, Phone, Instagram/Facebook/LinkedIn/TikTok/YouTube/Twitter / X, Website, Full Address/Suburb/City/State/Postcode/Country/Country Code, Niche (+Group), Segment, ICP Score /10, Tier, Revenue Band, Lead Insight, Status, My Notes, Lead Added On, Last Checked, Data Source, Found On, Place Id. 'Place Id' is the stable dedupe key (forms: Google ChIJ..., osm:node/N, yt:UC..., input:<md5>, gmapscid:<cid>, imp:<md5>; CONTRACT.md wrongly says import:...). Country is a full name ('United States') plus an ISO-2 'Country Code'; YouTube rows may have both blank. State is an abbreviation for Google/US/AU data but free text elsewhere (England, Dubai, Riyadh...). 'City' is the SEARCH city, not necessarily the business city ('Suburb' comes from the address).
3) Dates are TEXT, date-only: 'Lead Added On' and 'Last Checked' = YYYY-MM-DD in the sheet's Rules>TIMEZONE (default UTC worldwide, Australia/Sydney in the AU edition), written with valueInputOption RAW. There is no time-of-day on any lead row, so 'leads per hour', 'time of arrival' and live 'today' must come from the Database app's own first-seen timestamp when it polls. Only Run Log / Stats / Meta carry 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC' timestamps. The only per-lead timezone is the AU edition's 'AU Timezone' column (IANA name derived from state).
4) Append-only is the core contract: the lead bot only adds rows below the last used row (computed from watched columns: Place Id, Company Name, Niche, Status, My Notes, Website, Segment, Lead Added On and ANY column not in its own header list), via an explicit range update (A<last+1>), never sorts/inserts/deletes/rewrites a lead row, and 'Status' is written once as 'New'. Status/My Notes belong to the user; the outreach bot may set Status (New, Drafted, Contacted, Follow-up 1, Follow-up 2, Replied, Call booked, Client, Not interested, Do not contact) and add columns prefixed 'Outreach '. Rows are written per search DURING a ~42-minute job (twice a day), so a 1-2 minute rescan will see rows arrive in bursts of roughly 2-6 rows per search.
5) Dashboards inside the sheets: Stats/US Stats (A1 title; rows 3-8 = Total leads, Leads today (date), PRIME leads, Last run, Run health, Keys registered; header row 10; one row per niche from row 11 with Total/Today/PRIME/PRIME-REVIEW/GROWING/HAS-AGENCY/POLISHED/Share(formula)/Progress(SPARKLINE formula)) and the Master Dashboard (header row 11, per-sheet rows from 12, then a per-niche table). They are overwritten in place every run with USER_ENTERED formulas, so the Database app should never write there. The hidden 'Meta' tab (Key/Value) holds a 'summary' JSON {date, tabs:{tab:{total,today,prime,segs}}}, last_run, health and a write 'lock'; reading 'Meta' is the cheapest way to get totals, but it refreshes only at the end of each run.
6) Volume is ESTIMATED, not measured on real sheets: worldwide about 250-400 leads/day for the first 3-4 weeks (US 70-100, AU 70-100, UK 40-70, CA 40-70, NZ 25-40, IE 15-30, YouTube 5-15) then 25-60/day; AU-only 250-400/day for ~2 weeks then 30-60. Runs: worldwide cron 08:00 and 20:00 UTC, AU-only 07:00 and 19:00 UTC. PROGRESS.md still lists 'Verify the daily Actions run fills the sheets', and no real lead sheet, local_sheet folder or sample lead CSV exists on disk, so real column fill rates and row counts are unknown.
7) Niches (30 enabled of 35 worldwide rows; 27 of 31 in AU) include surgeons, dentists, clinics, real estate, buyers agents, mortgage brokers, migration/law firms, accountants, furniture/kitchen showrooms, car/boat dealers, builders/architects, solar, pool/landscape, wedding venues, private colleges, hair transplant, jewellers, boutique hotels, childcare, boutique gyms, fine dining groups, plus 3-4 YouTube-creator niches. Countries: US, CA, UK, AU, NZ, IE (+AE, SA, QA optional) with 97 seeded search areas (AU 39, US 23, UK 12, CA 7, NZ 4, AE 4, IE 3, SA 3, QA 2). The bot's own ICP score is /10 with gate 7 (MIN_ICP_SCORE), so 'quality vs their ICP' already exists as 'ICP Score /10', 'Tier' (A>=8.5, B>=7.5, else C) and 'Segment' (PRIME, PRIME-REVIEW, GROWING, HAS-AGENCY, POLISHED-NO-SIGNAL).
8) The other automations do not produce lead sheets in the same shape: IG outreach writes 'Outreach Log' (29 cols), 'Today Queue' (14), 'Accounts' (7), 'Run Log' (3) and READS a user-pasted leads tab (first tab of its sheet unless LEADS_TAB is set) with fuzzy substring header matching; its dates are '04-Nov-2026' style (DATE_FORMAT) plus ISO and 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm' stamps from an Apps Script. sheet-organizer is a notes/tasks organizer (Inbox -> Tasks, Problems, Achievements, Ideas, Resources, Attention Needed, Monthly Summary, _Ledger), not lead gen. Scraper Tools output CSV/JSON files (gosom 36-column CSV, yt-dlp 8-column CSV, crawl4ai JSON) that feed the lead bot's importer, not Google Sheets. local-drafter reads any lead sheet with an auto column mapper and writes 'Ready to Send' (Email, First Name, Subject, Body in A-D only), 'Log', 'Needs Review'. The Full Cycle Emails folder holds only a build prompt (spec for the Outreach email app, which reads 5-7 source sheets read-only).
9) Biggest risks if the Database app WROTE into lead sheets: (a) any cell it writes in a non-bot column below the data, or a formula/ARRAYFORMULA column that extends rows, moves the 'last used row' and the bot then appends after it, leaving gaps; (b) a header with the same name as a bot column (Status, Country, Notes...) gets the bot's value written into BOTH columns; (c) renaming/deleting 'Place Id', 'Company Name' or 'Lead Insight' headers makes the bot append a fresh header at the end and lose its in-sheet dedupe; (d) inserting a title row above row 1 breaks lead-tab detection (row 1 only); (e) creating tabs with reserved names (stats, meta, dashboard, summary, rules, seen, run log, etc.) collides with bot tabs, and the bot reorders tabs each run; (f) the bot writes with an explicit-range update, so a row appended by another writer between its re-read and its write can be overwritten (the AU-only edition runs jobs one at a time for exactly this reason); (g) shared service-account quota (60 reads/min and 60 writes/min per user per project, 300/min per project) is already used by the lead bot (~15 reads/min peak) and outreach bot (<=19 reads/min). Recommendation: treat lead sheets as read-only, keep all Database-app state (assignment, access, delete requests, soft-delete flags) in the app's own database, use a separate service account/GCP project, and poll with 1 metadata call + 1 batchGet of only the needed columns per sheet.

pitfalls: APPEND POSITION CORRUPTION: the lead bot computes the next row from the longest 'watched' column (its own key columns plus ANY header not in its list, e.g. a Database-app column like 'Assigned To'). If the app writes values or fills a formula/ARRAYFORMULA down many rows in a non-bot column, the bot appends below that, leaving blank gaps (LB\src\leadbot.py:1219-1225, 1305).

DUPLICATE HEADER NAMES: rows are built as [cell(l.get(h)) for h in hdr], so if the app adds a column whose header equals a bot header (Status, Notes, Country, City, Phone, Email, Niche...), the bot writes its value into BOTH columns. Any app-added column must use a unique prefix (e.g. 'DB ') (LB\src\leadbot.py:1315).

HEADER ROW IS ROW 1 ONLY: lead-tab detection, column mapping and header repair all read row 1. Inserting a title/banner row above it, merging row 1 cells, or renaming 'Place Id', 'Company Name' or 'Lead Insight' makes the bot re-append the header at the end (losing in-sheet dedupe) or ignore the tab (LB\src\leadbot.py:1257-1261, 1290-1291).

RACE ON WRITE: write_leads re-reads then updates an explicit range A<last+1>; a row appended by another writer inside that window is silently overwritten. The AU-only edition runs collect jobs one at a time for this reason (AU\AU_EDITION.md:15). The Database app must never append/insert rows in lead tabs; delete or sort would also shift rows while a job is mid-run.

RESERVED/OWNED TABS: the bot owns Stats, US Stats, Master Dashboard, Meta, Seen, Searches, Snapshots, Run Log, Rules, Niches, Locations, Options, Playbook, Import, Leads Input, Blacklist; creating an app tab with one of these names (or Dashboard/Summary/All Leads) collides, and order_tabs() pushes unknown tabs after the niche tabs on every run. Writing into Meta's 'lock' key blocks lead runs for up to 57 minutes. Stats and Master Dashboard are overwritten in place with formulas every run.

FIRST-TAB ASSUMPTION IN IG OUTREACH: ig-outreach reads leads from the FIRST worksheet unless LEADS_TAB is set (IG\main.py:155-157). Adding or reordering tabs in that sheet (e.g. a new Database tab at position 0) makes it read the wrong tab and fail with 'no Instagram/Handle column'. IG's Accounts/Today Queue/Outreach Log are updated in place by row index, so sorting or deleting rows there during a run corrupts syncing.

STATUS IS SHARED STATE: 'Status' is written by the lead bot ('New') and by the outreach bot (10 values); IG uses a different 'Lead Status' + 'Stage' vocabulary. If the Database app edits Status in sheets, the outreach bot's skip rules (Do not contact / Not interested) and IG's stop statuses are affected. Hosting/back-end limits for the Database.summary:
1) The existing FACTS-CHECKED.md (2026-11-03) already settled that Free pauses after 1 week idle, built-in SMTP is team-only at 2 emails/h, and single-session is Pro-only. It left two items open, now confirmed: Free allows 2 active projects, shared across every org you own or administer, and 500,000 Edge Function invocations/month. PRICES.md has no hosting rows, so everything below is new.
2) The 2-project cap is the first design constraint. LevelUp CRM already uses one hosted Free project (Mumbai) and Outreach plans Supabase too, so Database cannot get its own Free project. Options: one project with a schema per app (shared auth.users, quotas, backups and 500 MB), or one Pro org at $25/mo (about $45/mo for 3 Micro projects, my calculation).
3) For a business app the Free plan is risky: no backups at all, pausing after 7 days of low activity, and when over quota (after an unspecified grace period) Supabase can switch the DB to read-only or answer every API call with HTTP 402. Pro gives daily backups (7 days), no pausing, 8 GB disk, 250 GB egress and 2M invocations. PITR is about $100/mo extra.
4) Scan runner: pg_cron supports 1-59 second intervals (Postgres 15.1.1.61+) and no official page restricts it on Free. Edge Function limits are 2 s CPU (I/O wait not counted), 150 s wall clock on Free, 256 MB. One invocation per 1-minute tick is 43,200/month, 8.6% of the Free quota. Recommended: pg_cron every 60 s, then pg_net, then one Edge Function that returns fast and works in EdgeRuntime.waitUntil, with a lease table, incremental range reads and a heartbeat alert.
5) The binding limit is Google, not Supabase: Sheets API allows 60 reads/min per user per project (a service account counts as one user) and 300/min per project. That is about 50 sheets at a 1-minute cadence or about 100 at 2 minutes, one read per sheet per tick. Drive modifiedTime/push is coalesced and may lag about 3 minutes (a 2020 Google-staff answer, not re-verified), so do not use it to skip reads.
6) Rejected runners: GitHub Actions (5-minute minimum, delays of 15-60 minutes and hours reported, jobs may be dropped); Vercel Hobby (cron once per day with +-59 min precision, and commercial use banned); Cloudflare Workers Free cron (10 ms CPU, 50 subrequests, 5 triggers per account). Workers Paid ($5/mo) would work. A Hetzner VPS (about EUR 5.49-5.99/mo) is the robust fallback and the Outreach plan already includes one, so the scan could share it.
7) Hosting the web app: Cloudflare Pages Free allows commercial use (no non-commercial clause in the Self-Serve Subscription Agreement or the Service-Specific Terms). Limits are 500 builds per month (not per day), 20,000 files, 25 MiB per file, and unlimited static bandwidth. Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only, so Pro at $20 per deploying seat is needed.
8) Storage math at 1.5 KB per lead (assumption, not measured): 500 MB holds about 333,000 leads (decimal) or 341,000 (binary). After the 40-60 MB fresh-project baseline, about 300,000. Growth is 7.5, 30 and 90 MB/month at 5k, 20k and 60k new leads/month, so 450 MB fills in 60, 15 and 5 months (with a 30% reserve: 42, 10.5, 3.5). Pro 8 GB gives about 5.6M leads.
9) Realtime Free limits (200 connections, 100 msg/s) are ample for a small team. RLS is not applied to DELETE events, so the fail-safe delete rule must live in RLS/RPC and must not rely on Realtime. Deleting rows does not shrink the DB without VACUUM, so use soft-delete.

facts.fact: Supabase Free quotas: DB 500 MB per project, egress 5 GB, storage 1 GB, 50,000 MAU, 500,000 Edge Function invocations, Realtime 200 peak connections and 2M messages, log retention 1 day. Pro: 8 GB disk per project (then $0.125/GB), 250 GB egress ($0.09/GB beyond), 100 GB storage, 100,000 MAU, 2M invocations ($2 per million beyond), Realtime 500 connections and 5M messages, 7-day logs.

The 500 MB figure is a billing quota, not a disk trigger. Free projects have a fixed 2 GB disk and go read-only at 95% disk. WAL counts toward disk but not DB size. A fresh project already uses about 40-60 MB. DB size counts data, indexes and materialized views.

Exceeding Free quotas: notice, then a grace period of unspecified length, then Fair Use restrictions that can pause projects, switch DBs to read-only, or answer all API requests with HTTP 402. Upgrading to Pro lifts them immediately. The docs do not say data is deleted.

Pausing: Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity; paid orgs are never paused for inactivity. What counts as activity is not defined officially; community replies disagree (any API request vs a real DB write; pg_cron counts per one unofficial reply). A scheduled-job DB is unavailable while paused.

Backups: Free none (pricing 'Not included'; backups doc says daily backups cover Pro/Team/Enterprise and tells Free users to export with 'supabase db dump'; going-into-prod: backups not available for download on Free). Pro: daily, 7 days; Team 14 days. PITR add-on about $100/mo per 7 days (EUR/USD per doc table: $0.137/h, $200 for 14 d, $400 for 28 d), needs at least Small compute, RPO 2 minutes, and enabling PITR stops daily backups.

Pro cost: from $25/month per org, includes $10 compute credit (covers one Micro). Compute: Nano $0 (Free only, shared CPU, up to 0.5 GB RAM, 60 direct connections, pooler 200 clients, default pool 15), Micro about $10/mo (1 GB), Small about $15/mo (2 GB). Pro spend cap is on by default. Calculation: 3 separate Micro projects on one Pro org = $25 + 3x$10 - $10 = about $45/mo before overage; one shared project = $25/mo.

Edge Function limits (hosted): memory 256 MB; CPU 2 s per request (async I/O wait does not count); wall clock Free 150 s / Paid 400 s; request idle timeout 150 s (504); function size 20 MB (CLI bundle) or 5 MB (server-side bundle); 100 functions per project on Free (Pro 1,000). Request/response body limits are not documented.

Edge Functions can keep running after responding via EdgeRuntime.waitUntil(promise) until the promise ends, but are capped by the same wall-clock, CPU and memory limits; a beforeunload listener fires before shutdown.

Supabase Cron (pg_cron): enabled under Integrations > Cron; docs list no plan restriction. Supports 5-field cron (1-minute precision) and '[1-59] seconds' intervals on Postgres 15.1.1.61 or later; seconds cannot be mixed with other units. Recommended max 8 concurrent jobs (pg_cron default cron.max_running_jobs = 32) and max 10 min per job. Only one instance of a given job runs at a time; overlaps are queued. No retries. cron.job_run_details is never cleaned automatically.

pg_cron on Free: no official restriction found and a Supabase GitHub thread says cron is limited only by CPU/memory/disk, but one Free user reported a job that showed as scheduled and never ran (cause not a plan limit). Prior Outreach research also flagged it as not explicitly documented. Treat as 'very likely works, verify with a pilot'.

pg_net: async HTTP from SQL, beta ('function signatures may change'); about 200 requests/second; default timeout 2000 ms (the cron quickstart example sets timeout_milliseconds 5000); responses kept 6 hours in net._http_response; request/response tables are unlogged (lost on crash); no bounded retries; request only starts after the transaction commits; max body size not stated.

Official pattern to schedule an Edge Function: put project_url and secret key in Vault, cron.schedule(...) calling net.http_post with header apikey = secret key (not the publishable key), function with verify_jwt disabled and auth 'secret'. Warning: while a request is queued the decrypted key is visible in net.http_request_queue to any DB login role.

Invocations math (my calculation): one invocation per tick = 43,200/month at 1 min (8.6% of the 500k Free quota), 21,600 at 2 min, 86,400 at 30 s. Fan-out of 3 chunks per tick = 129,600/month at 1 min; 5 chunks = 216,000. Whether cron/pg_net-triggered calls count toward the quota is not stated in the docs (assume yes).

facts.fact: Realtime limits (Free / Pro / Team): concurrent connections 200 / 500 / 10,000; messages per second 100 / 500 / 2,500; channel joins per second 100 / 500 / 2,500; channels per connection 100; presence messages per second 20 / 50 / 1,000; broadcast payload 256 KB / 3,000 KB; Postgres Changes payload 1,024 KB.

Realtime Postgres Changes: processed on a single thread, authorizes every event for every subscriber, so throughput scales with subscribers; larger compute does not help; with RLS on a Micro, max about 3,000 msg/s at 500 clients. RLS policies are NOT applied to DELETE events; filtering deletes needs REPLICA IDENTITY FULL. Supabase advises Broadcast for large fan-out.

Auth rate limits: built-in email provider 2 emails/hour project-wide, only to team members, not configurable. With custom SMTP the default is 30 emails/hour, adjustable on the Rate Limits page. Per-user password reset /recover: 1 request per 60 s. Per IP: sign-up/in/recover/otp 30 per 5 min; /token 150 per 5 min; /verify 30 per 5 min; OTP 360/hour default; MFA 15/min; anonymous 30/hour. Exceeding returns 429. Custom SMTP is required for production; Resend, AWS SES, Postmark, SendGrid, ZeptoMail, Brevo are the listed providers.
Storage on Free: 1 GB total and a 50 MB global per-file limit (Pro can raise to 500 GB).

RLS performance rules from Supabase: wrap auth.uid() as (select auth.uid()) so it becomes an initPlan evaluated once; index every column used in a policy (must be the leading column of a btree; a composite PK does not index later columns); put per-sheet access checks in a SECURITY DEFINER helper with pinned search_path; always add 'to authenticated' so the policy skips other roles; avoid policies that recurse into each other.

Several apps in one Supabase project is workable: one schema per app, add each schema to Exposed schemas and run the documented GRANT USAGE/ALL statements (plus ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES), RLS per schema. Shared by all apps: auth.users, storage, keys, quotas, backups, one migration history, 500 MB. Grants without RLS expose tables to anon/authenticated.

Connections: on Free the direct Postgres connection is IPv6-only; the shared pooler is IPv4. Transaction mode (port 6543) is recommended for serverless/edge, and prepared statements must be off there. Data API (supabase-js) is recommended for browsers.

facts.fact: Sheets read budget (my calculation): at 1 read per sheet per tick and 60 reads/min per service account, about 50 sheets fit at a 1-minute cadence (10 reads headroom for retries) and about 100 sheets at a 2-minute cadence if requests are spread across the window. More sheets need a longer cadence, quota increase or more service accounts/projects (quota-increase path exists per Google; multi-account approach not verified against ToS).

pitfalls: Only 2 active Free projects per user across all orgs you own/admin; CRM already uses one and Outreach will want one, so a third Free project is impossible. Creating more orgs does not help.

Free plan has no backups and pauses after 1 week of low activity. If the scan stops, leads from the gap are still in the sheets but dashboards go stale. Pro ($25/mo) fixes pausing and gives 7-day daily backups.

Over the 500 MB quota the grace period is unspecified, after which Supabase may pause, go read-only or return HTTP 402 on all API calls. Set an alert at about 350 MB (70%) and never run production near the limit.
cron.job_run_details is never auto-cleaned: 43,200 rows/month at a 1-minute cadence. Add a daily cleanup job or the history table eats the 500 MB.

pg_net is beta, has no retries, uses unlogged tables lost on crash, and its default timeout is 2000 ms (cron quickstart example uses 5000). pg_cron only prevents overlap of the cron job itself, not of the async Edge Function, so add a lease/lock row so two scans never write the same sheet at once.

Edge Function CPU is 2 s per request and 150 s wall clock on Free. Initial backfill of a large sheet must be chunked with a saved cursor (for example 2,000-5,000 rows per tick). Never read a whole 60k-row sheet in one invocation. Exceeding limits ends the worker (resource-limit error, code 546 per Supabase troubleshooting index, article not read).

Google Sheets quota is 60 reads/min per user per project, and a service account is one user. 429 means back off for 1 minute. Spread the sheet reads across the minute instead of bursting, and batch ranges per spreadsheet (a batch counts as 1 request, but only within one spreadsheet).

Do not use Drive modifiedTime or Drive push notifications as the change detector for a 1-minute SLA: they can lag about 3 minutes, push is coalesced, channels expire after at most 1 day for files and need manual renewal, and modifiedTime also changes for formatting edits. Detect new rows by reading the tail range (last_row+1 onward) instead.
Sheets onEdit (Apps Script) does not fire for API or automation writes (common knowledge, not verified here), so it cannot replace polling for n8n/Make-filled sheets.

Realtime Postgres Changes is single-threaded and checks RLS per subscriber, and RLS is not applied to DELETE events. Do not enforce the admin-only-delete rule through Realtime. Use RLS DELETE policy admin-only plus a deletion_requests table and an approve RPC, and prefer soft-delete (deleted_at).
Deleting rows does not free disk quickly: VACUUM is needed and VACUUM FULL locks the table. Soft-delete and archive instead of mass hard-deletes.

Reset emails: built-in Supabase SMTP only reaches project team members at 2/hour. Custom SMTP is mandatory for employee reset codes, with a default of 30 emails/hour (adjustable). CRM is still blocked on SMTP_PASS (PROGRESS.md line 14), so reuse the same SMTP setup.

Vercel Hobby bans commercial use (including a paid employee or consultant writing the code) and limits cron to once per day with +-59 min timing. Cloudflare Workers cron config changes take up to 15 min to propagate and run in UTC only.
GitHub Actions schedule: public-repo schedules are auto-disabled after 60 days without repo activity, and runs only on the default branch.

Service key in a cron job: store it in Vault and call the function with the secret key (not the publishable key). While a pg_net request is queued the decrypted key sits in net.http_request_queue and is readable by any DB login role.

The 1.5 KB/lead figure is an assumption. Measure with 10,000 synthetic rows and pg_total_relation_size before trusting the months-to-full table. Also count audit log, session, request and cron-history tables against the same 500 MB.
Single shared project means shared auth.users: the single-active-session logic (own active_sessions table, per FACTS-CHECKED.md) and role claims must be namespaced per app if apps are combined.

Third-party claim (sheet2api, 2026-10) that Google will start billing over-quota Sheets API use later in 2026 conflicts with Google's cached page ('no charges'). Not verified; re-check the live page before launch.

Google-side design for polling many bot-.area: Google-side design for polling many bot-filled Google Sheets every 1-2 minutes (Sheets API quotas, Drive change detection, Apps Script alternative, service-account sharing, concurrency, large tabs). All sources checked 2026-11-04.
Google-side design for polling many bot-.summary:
KEY FINDINGS. (1) Sheets API quota is 300 reads/min/project and 60 reads/min/user/project, same for writes. All calls from one service account count as ONE user, so the 60/min bucket is the real ceiling, not 300. A batch (batchGet) counts as one request regardless of ranges. 429 means wait for the minute refill, exponential backoff with jitter. No daily cap, but Google says exceeding quota is planned to be billed later in 2026. (2) Cheapest change gate is Drive: one files.list (100 quota units, up to 1000 files, with modifiedTime/version in fields) or changes.list (100 units, reports removed=true on deletion or loss of access) against a 1,000,000 units/min project budget, so polling Drive every minute is effectively free. headRevisionId does NOT work for Sheets (binary files only). Freshness is the weak point: the only evidence on lag is a 2020 Google-engineer reply that Drive push for Sheets is coalesced to roughly every 3 minutes; whether a bot's API append bumps modifiedTime promptly is NOT documented and NOT verified. (3) Drive push (files.watch max 1 day, changes.watch max 7 days, no auto-renew, empty-body notifications, public HTTPS with valid cert) works but is coalesced, needs renewal jobs, and still needs a follow-up read. Workspace Events API for Drive (folder subscription with includeDescendants, Pub/Sub, user OAuth, 7-day TTL) is still Developer Preview per the sources found; do not build on it. (4) Apps Script is a poor fit: Google documents that script executions and API requests do NOT fire triggers, so onEdit never fires for bot writes; onChange for API writes is contradicted by community reports; it needs a script plus installable trigger plus authorization inside every sheet; consumer quotas are 90 min/day trigger runtime and 20,000 URL fetches/day shared per user. (5) Sharing is file-level (no per-tab access); a Viewer share of the sheet or its folder gives the service account every tab. Sharing with a whole domain does NOT reach service accounts. Use spreadsheets.readonly (+ drive.metadata.readonly for Drive metadata). Permission loss: Sheets returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED for an unshared spreadsheet (single third-party live test), 404 NOT_FOUND for a wrong id; Drive returns 404 for files you cannot see; changes feed gives removed=true. (6) Rows have no stable IDs; gridProperties.rowCount is grid size, not last data row; developer metadata follows rows on insert but needs Editor access, has a 30,000-char budget per sheet, and sort behaviour is undocumented. (7) values.append is NOT documented as concurrency-safe: Google (2016) confirmed concurrent appends can overwrite each other; safest is not to write into bot-owned tabs at all. (8) Large tabs: read only a window after the last seen row (trailing empty rows are omitted, so A{n+1}:Z returns nothing when idle), keep payloads near 2 MB, chunk full re-syncs, and hash client-side (Sheets has no server-side checksum).

DESIGN IMPLICATIONS. 1) Keep ALL app state (assignments, employee-added leads, delete requests, soft-deletes) in the app's own database; treat bot sheets as read-only sources and share them as Viewer. This sidesteps append races and makes the delete fail-safe fully app-enforced. 2) Poll loop every 60s: one Drive files.list (mimeType spreadsheet, fields id,modifiedTime,version,trashed) or changes.list for all sheets; for sheets whose modifiedTime moved, do ONE values.batchGet covering all their tabs (1 Sheets read per changed spreadsheet). Budget: stay under about 45 Sheets reads/min with one service account; serialise to at most 1 request/second per spreadsheet. 3) Because modifiedTime may lag minutes and API-write behaviour is unverified, add a safety net: force a cheap tail-read of every sheet every 5-10 min (or of recently active sheets every minute) and measure real lag in a pilot before promising 1-2 min SLAs. 4) Identify rows by content key (lead email+phone+timestamp or the bot's own ID column) plus an anchor check (re-read the last seen row and compare a hash); on mismatch fall back to a chunked full resync, because bots may insert, delete or sort. Never store row numbers as identity. 5) Per tab keep lastSeenRow, anchor hash, sheetId (stable, immutable) and tab title; get tabs via spreadsheets.get with a fields mask (sheetId,title,hidden,gridProperties) and the sheet timeZone/locale; do not trust rowCount as data size. 6) Use UNFORMATTED_VALUE with FORMATTED_STRING dates (or SERIAL_NUMBER) so locale does not change parsing, and compute leads today/week/month in each sheet's own timeZone. 7) Detect permission loss via changes.list removed=true, files.list no longer returning the file, and Sheets 403/404 confirmed with Drive files.get; surface per-sheet status in the admin portal. 8) Optional true push: add a final HTTP node in each automation that pings the Database app webhook after it appends (inference, not Google-documented); skip Apps Script. 9) Add a global token-bucket limiter, exponential backoff with jitter on 429/500/503, and a quota counter in the UI; plan for Google billing for over-quota use later in 2026 and for separate service accounts only after testing whether each gets its own per-user bucket. 10) If writing back to Sheets is ever required, use a separate app-owned spreadsheet, append-only with insertDataOption INSERT_ROWS, valueInputOption RAW for phones, a single writer queue, and a client-generated row ID for dedupe.

NOT CHECKED / SKIPPED: I ran no live API test (read-only, no credentials), so modifiedTime latency, onChange behaviour, per-service-account quota, and sort effects on metadata are untested. Risk: Google quota and billing pages are changing in 2026; re-check the Cloud console values for your own project.

facts.fact: Sheets API quotas: read 300/min/project and 60/min/user/project; write 300/min/project and 60/min/user/project; refilled every minute; over quota returns 429 'Too many requests'; no daily request cap while within per-minute quotas.

Google states API calls by a service account are considered to be using a single account, so all app traffic through one service account shares the 60/min per-user bucket (the dev.to author hit the per-user limit, not the project limit).
Each batch request, including any subrequest, counts as one API request toward the quota (so values.batchGet over many ranges/tabs of one spreadsheet = 1 read).

429 handling: truncated exponential backoff (wait 1,2,4s... plus random up to 1000 ms, capped typically at 32 or 64 s); page says requests can resume after 1 minute. No Retry-After header is documented. Per-user 429 message text: "Quota exceeded for quota metric 'Read requests' and limit 'Read requests per minute per user' of service 'sheets.googleapis.com'"; status RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
No hard payload limit but Google recommends a 2 MB maximum payload; requests processed for more than 180 seconds return a timeout error.

503 guidance for large/complex sheets: limit concurrent requests per spreadsheet to 1 request per second; retrieve only needed values via A1 ranges; restrict includeGridData; use field masks; exponential backoff; 500 = API-side issue (file bug).

Pricing/quota-increase: standard Sheets API use is free; exceeding quota is 'planned to incur charges to your Google Cloud billing account later in 2026'; quota adjustments can be requested in Cloud console 'Quotas & System Limits', approval not guaranteed.

Spreadsheet size cap is up to 20 million cells (doubled from 10 million), GA announced 2026-09-10 with up to 15 days rollout, applies to new, existing and imported files; imported-file byte limit increase is 'coming soon'. Some third-party sites still say 10 million. Column cap of 18,278 (ZZZ) appears only in secondary sources (not verified officially).

values.get reads one range; values.batchGet reads many discontinuous ranges in one call (no max range count stated in docs). valueRenderOption default FORMATTED_VALUE (formatted using the SPREADSHEET's locale, not the requester's); UNFORMATTED_VALUE returns raw numbers; FORMULA returns formulas. dateTimeRenderOption default SERIAL_NUMBER (days since 1899-12-30) and only matters when valueRenderOption is not FORMATTED_VALUE; FORMATTED_STRING gives locale-formatted strings. Trailing empty rows/columns are omitted from reads.

Partial responses: 'fields' parameter works on any request that returns data (comma list, a/b nesting, parentheses sub-select); gzip via 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' plus 'gzip' in User-Agent reduces bandwidth.

Real-world large read: a 10 columns x 1,000,000 rows sheet fetched with one values.get failed with 'response too large'; chunked reads of 200,000 rows took about 45 s via the Sheets API (Apps Script test, 2022-04-25).

Drive API quota (quota-unit model): 1,000,000 units/min/project; 325,000 units/min/user/project; 400,000,000 units/day/project billing threshold; costs: files.get 5, files.list 100, changes.list 100, files.watch 100, changes.watch 100, changes.getStartPageToken 5, edits 50, downloads/exports 200. Cloud projects created on/after 2026-05-01 use the new quotas; projects with Drive API use between Nov 2025 and Apr 2026 keep their earlier quotas. Exceeding is planned to be charged later in 2026.

Drive rate errors: 403 userRateLimitExceeded / rateLimitExceeded and 429 rateLimitExceeded, all retried with exponential backoff; JSON error body is {error:{code,message,errors:[{domain,reason,message}]}}. 404 notFound means file does not exist OR caller lacks read access; 403 insufficientFilePermissions means no edit permission.

Drive File fields: modifiedTime = last time modified by anyone (RFC 3339); version = monotonically increasing number reflecting every server-side change, even ones not visible to the user; headRevisionId is only available for files with binary content, so it is unusable for Google Sheets files.

files.list: pageSize max 1000 (default whole list for non-shared drives); orderBy modifiedTime desc supported; q supports modifiedTime > 'RFC3339' (default UTC), mimeType, trashed, 'id' in parents, sharedWithMe. One files.list call with fields mask can return id/modifiedTime/version for all shared sheets.

changes feed: getStartPageToken then changes.list (oldest first, pageSize max 1000, store newStartPageToken); Change.removed is true when a file was removed from the list 'for example by deletion or loss of access' (needs includeRemoved); restrictToMyDrive must be false to see shared files; the change log keeps only one entry per file. Whether a service account's feed includes files shared with it is implied but not explicitly documented.

Drive push notifications: only files.watch and changes.watch; receiver must be HTTPS with valid (non-self-signed) certificate; channel id max 64 chars, optional token max 256 chars (echoed as X-Goog-Channel-Token); files channels max 1 day, changes channels max 1 week, default 1 hour; no automatic renewal (create a new channel with a new id before expiry); a 'sync' message arrives first; notifications have empty body and need follow-up files.get / changes.list; states for files: sync, add, remove, update, trash, untrash.

Domain verification for the webhook domain: fast.io says verify in Search Console and register in Cloud Console; the official push page only states the HTTPS/valid-certificate requirement. Conflict, not verified.

Latency of Drive push / modifiedTime for Sheets: a Google engineer (sqrrrl) wrote 2020-01-21 that there is no real-time API and Drive push updates for sheets are coalesced and sent roughly every ~3 minutes; the reporter said Drive modifiedTime refreshes at the same ~3 min cadence. Only evidence found; 2020, not re-verified in 2026. No official doc states the delay. Sheets API v4 exposes no modified time (must use Drive).
Revisions for Docs/Sheets/Slides may be merged, so the revisions API does not show every edit; revisions are content-only while changes include metadata. Revisions are unsuitable as an edit counter.

Workspace Events API Drive subscriptions: added as Developer Preview 2025-07-07; supports contentChanged-type events, folder/shared-drive targets with includeDescendants, delivery to Pub/Sub, normally user OAuth (authorizing user must have access), 7-day max TTL in a June 2026 tutorial that still calls it Developer Public Preview; at-least-once, unordered. One web summary claimed GA but fetched release notes show only Developer Preview, so GA status is not verified.

Official: 'Script executions and API requests don't cause triggers to run' (only exception named: Form.submitGrades()). So onEdit/installable onEdit do not fire for edits made by bots through the Sheets API. Google engineer also said onEdit fires only for interactive UI edits (2020).

Installable onChange (Sheets only) event has changeType (EDIT, INSERT_ROW, INSERT_COLUMN, REMOVE_ROW, REMOVE_COLUMN, INSERT_GRID, REMOVE_GRID, FORMAT, OTHER) but no range/value. Whether it fires for Sheets API writes is contradicted: Google Groups thread (2022-07-12) says neither onChange nor onEdit fire for API writes; a Tanaike gist (2022-11-10) says OnChange detects Sheets API edits by a service account (service-account email missing from event). Not verified.

Apps Script quotas (per user, reset 24 h after first request): Triggers total runtime 90 min/day consumer vs 6 h/day Workspace; URL Fetch calls 20,000/day consumer vs 100,000/day Workspace; script runtime 6 min/execution; 30 simultaneous executions per user; 20 triggers per user per script; URL Fetch POST/response up to 50 MB. Quota is shared across all of a user's scripts. Quotas may change without notice.

Time-driven triggers can run as often as every minute. Simple triggers cannot use services that require authorization (so UrlFetchApp webhooks need installable triggers), run max 30 s, and the page notes onEdit queues only up to 2 trigger events.

Sharing: add the service account's unique email in the Share dialog as Viewer/Commenter/Editor like a user; sharing a Workspace asset with the whole domain does NOT share it with service accounts. Sheets scopes apply to the spreadsheet file, not individual sheets (permissions are file-level; no per-tab access). Folder permissions are inherited by children. Viewer vs hidden tabs: sources conflict; Sheets API exposes SheetProperties.hidden.

Scopes: Sheets API spreadsheets.readonly is 'sensitive'; Drive scopes drive.metadata.readonly / drive.readonly / drive are 'restricted'; drive.file only covers files the app created or opened (a web summary says shared files then 404, not directly verified). Restricted-scope verification applies to OAuth consent apps; whether it applies to a key-based service account is not verified.

Permission-loss error shapes: a live test dated 2026-10-06 (single third-party report) found Sheets API on a spreadsheet the caller cannot see returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED 'The caller does not have permission' (errors[0].reason forbidden), while a nonexistent id (or a hidden Doc read via Sheets) returns 404 NOT_FOUND 'Requested entity was not found.' (reason notFound). Google's Sheets troubleshooting page does not document 403/404. Drive docs say 404 covers both missing and no-read-access. 403 can also mean API not enabled or wrong scope.

Cheap tab list: spreadsheets.get with a fields mask returns sheets.properties (sheetId immutable and non-negative, title, index, hidden, sheetType, gridProperties.rowCount/columnCount) plus spreadsheet properties.timeZone (CLDR, e.g. America/New_York) and locale; grid data is excluded by default. gridProperties.rowCount is documented only as 'number of rows in the grid' (grid size including blank rows), NOT the last row with data; last data row must come from a values read (trailing empties omitted).
Rows have no unique ID: cells are identified by row/column coordinates only; sheetId and spreadsheetId are stable across renames.

DeveloperMetadata: can attach key/value to a single row, column, sheet or spreadsheet; metadata stays with its row when rows are inserted above (row 5 becomes row 6); deleted when its row/object is deleted; storage budget 30,000 characters per spreadsheet plus 30,000 per sheet (so it cannot tag 50k rows); created via spreadsheets.batchUpdate (needs write access, Viewer creation not stated); DOCUMENT vs PROJECT visibility; behaviour on sortRange is not documented.

values.append: finds a 'table' in the given range and writes to the next row of the table starting at its first column; with only a sheet name it uses the LAST table; insertDataOption default OVERWRITE overwrites existing data after the table (may add rows at the end), INSERT_ROWS inserts new rows; valueInputOption RAW stores strings unparsed (a leading '=' stays text), USER_ENTERED parses like typing (dates, formulas, number formats inferred); response includes tableRange. AppendCellsRequest 'adds new cells after the last row with data'.

Concurrency: Google's Eric Koleda wrote 2016-10-06 that concurrent append requests are a known limitation because append writes into existing cells so two requests can hit the same cells and overwrite each other (the reporter lost 1 of 4 simultaneous rows); workarounds: application-level locking, or one batchUpdate with insertDimension + updateCells. batchUpdate is applied atomically in order and all-or-nothing, but 'not guaranteed' to reflect exactly your changes when collaborators edit. Official append docs contain no concurrency statement; whether INSERT_ROWS fully avoids the race is not documented.

ProtectedRange: protects a range or whole sheet; fields include editors (users, groups, domainUsersCanEdit), warningOnly (everyone can edit but gets a warning; editors ignored), requestingUserCanEdit (read-only); editors list is only visible to users with edit access. Protection restricts edits only, viewers still see everything.
Sheets API release notes 2025-2026 show no change-notification/watch feature; 2026 additions are comments (GA 2026-09-30), Sheets MCP server preview (2026-07-13), tables API (2025-04-29).

pitfalls: The binding quota is the per-user 60 reads/min bucket (one service account = one user), not the 300/min project cap; 30+ sheets polled naively every minute plus tab/metadata calls will exceed it.
Do not use Drive headRevisionId for Sheets (binary files only) and do not rely on revisions as an edit counter (they are merged).

Drive modifiedTime/push freshness for Sheets is unproven: only a 2020 Google reply says about 3 minutes; a bot API append may not move modifiedTime quickly. Gating reads purely on modifiedTime can silently miss new leads; keep a periodic tail-read safety net.

onEdit never fires for API/bot writes (official); onChange for API writes is contested; Apps Script installs per sheet, needs authorization in each, and consumer quotas (90 min/day triggers, 20,000 URL fetches/day) are shared across all of an owner's scripts.

Drive watch channels expire (files 1 day, changes 7 days, default 1 hour), are not auto-renewed and give no expiry warning; notifications carry no data and need a public HTTPS endpoint with a valid certificate.
gridProperties.rowCount is grid size, not data size; do not use it to detect new rows.

Row numbers are not identities: bots can insert, delete or sort and shift everything; developer metadata needs Editor access, has a 30,000-char budget per sheet, and its sort behaviour is undocumented.

Appending into a bot-owned tab can overwrite or interleave with the bot's concurrent appends (Google-confirmed limitation); table detection can also land rows in the wrong place if the tab has gaps or multiple tables. Appends are not idempotent, so retries can duplicate rows (analysis, not a Google statement).
Sharing a sheet with the whole Workspace domain does not reach a service account; it must be shared by its exact email (or a shared folder).

404 vs 403 are not a clean signal: Drive uses 404 for 'missing or no access'; Sheets 403 for unshared is a single third-party test; 403 can also mean API disabled or wrong scope. Always confirm via Drive files.get/trashed and the changes feed removed flag.

FORMATTED_VALUE uses the spreadsheet's locale, so dates/numbers/phones can differ per sheet; use UNFORMATTED_VALUE with an explicit dateTimeRenderOption and the sheet's timeZone, and write phones with RAW.

Google says exceeding Sheets/Drive quotas is planned to be billed later in 2026 (Drive page: new projects since 2026-05-01 use quota-unit limits; older projects keep earlier limits); check your own project's console values.
Service-account JSON keys are a security risk; keep them only in .env/secret store, never in code or chat.
Single values.get on a very large tab can fail ('response too large' at about 10M cells) or time out (180 s); open-ended A:A reads on huge tabs have produced 500 errors in user reports.
